name: Hanging Leg Raise
cues: Hang with a firm grip and a still body
Keep your legs straight and together
Raise your feet to hip height or higher
Curl your pelvis up at the top
Lower slowly so you stop the swing

qa.note: Family review 2026-10-01 rated minor. repaired: see repair report | skeptic after repair: The motion is correct. Total flexion reaches 100 deg: hip 4 to 80, plus lumbar 16 and thoracic 4 of posterior curl, with pelvis tilt 0 to -26 (qa/out/F9/repair/802-hanging-leg-raise.qa.json rom). That puts the thighs about 15 deg above horizontal, inside the 90 to 110 research range. The centre of mass stays under the grips (forward offset 0.06 mm against 20 mm) and the trunk moves back 10 cm (pelvis.tz -0.165 to -0.061) to counter the legs, so nothing swings. Elbows are about 6 deg, legs straight and together (thigh overlap 40.9 mm against the 42 mm allowance, feet visibly together in the hero at t=0.5), overhand grip on the bar, bases in frame. The cues now match the loop. The owner should judge the new hip-flexor shorts tint (lead decision 3 in the repair report, not yet in PLAN.md). At 480 px it shows as two small red slashes at the front of the shorts (scratchpad r2-802-tint-t5.png) and can read like a stain. It only shows while the hip is open (bottom and eccentric) and hides in the fold at the top. The side view (review-figure/figure-802-side.png) is mostly blocked by the upright, but the hero is the shipping view. | skeptic after repair: The legs-together fix is confirmed. In front/figure-802-front.png at t=0.5 to 0.75 the feet are together and the legs straight, which matches the cue. Side sheet: straight legs go about 10 to 15 deg above horizontal, the pelvis curls, there is no swing, the overhand grip wraps the bar (hands/figure-802-wrist_R.png) and the station bases are in frame. The new hip-flexor tint shows as saturated, jagged red wedges on the front of the shorts (front t=0.5, hero t=0.25 to 0.75). The shape reads more like a stain than a muscle, so the owner should judge it. QA passes with the 42 mm thigh-to-thigh allowance (measured 40.9 mm).
